fanoutqa_012287.x:
Ryan Fitzpatrick :: Professional career :: Buffalo Bills :: 2012 season :: chunk_0008
Fitzpatrick returned as the Bills' starter in 2012, finishing with 3,400 passing yards, 24 touchdowns, and 16 interceptions to go along with 48 carries for 197 yards and a touchdown in 16 games and starts.[[47]](#cite_note-47)

Following Chan Gailey's firing after the season, Bills general manager [Buddy Nix](/wiki/Buddy_Nix "Buddy Nix") was the victim of a [prank call](/wiki/Prank_call "Prank call") in which he inadvertently revealed that he was unhappy with Fitzpatrick's contract, stating "we just can't afford to pay that kind of money for a guy who's fighting for probably a backup job". Shortly after the leaked phone call was reported on by *[Deadspin](/wiki/Deadspin "Deadspin")*, the team parted ways with Fitzpatrick, releasing him on March 12, 2013, before he was due a $3 million bonus.[[48]](#cite_note-48)[[49]](#cite_note-49)[[50]](#cite_note-50)

Jim Kenney was born on August 7, 1958, in the [Whitman](/wiki/Whitman,_Philadelphia "Whitman, Philadelphia") neighborhood of [South Philadelphia](/wiki/South_Philadelphia "South Philadelphia"). His father was a firefighter and his mother was a homemaker. His parents both worked second jobs to put Jim and his four siblings through private Catholic schools. In high school, Kenney was a newspaper deliveryman and busboy.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Kenney graduated from [Saint Joseph's Preparatory School](/wiki/Saint_Joseph%27s_Preparatory_School "Saint Joseph's Preparatory School") in 1976 and in 1980 received a [political science](/wiki/Political_science "Political science") [bachelor's degree](/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree") from [La Salle University](/wiki/La_Salle_University "La Salle University").[[3]](#cite_note-pbj-3) He was the first in his family to graduate from college.

Following the successful resolution of commercial and fishing disputes between [Virginia](/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") and Maryland at the [Mount Vernon Conference](/wiki/Mount_Vernon_Conference "Mount Vernon Conference") in 1785, Virginia called for a trade conference between all the states, set for September 1786 in [Annapolis, Maryland](/wiki/Annapolis,_Maryland "Annapolis, Maryland"), with an aim toward resolving further-reaching interstate commercial antagonisms. When the [convention](/wiki/Annapolis_Convention_(1786) "Annapolis Convention (1786)") failed for lack of attendance due to suspicions among most of the other states, [Alexander Hamilton](/wiki/Alexander_Hamilton "Alexander Hamilton") of New York led the Annapolis delegates in a call for a convention to offer revisions to the Articles, to be held the next spring in [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"). Prospects for the next convention appeared bleak until [James Madison](/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison") and [Edmund Randolph](/wiki/Edmund_Randolph "Edmund Randolph") succeeded in securing [George Washington](/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington")'s attendance to Philadelphia as a delegate for Virginia.[[22]](#cite_note-Milkis-26)[[26]](#cite_note-Beeman-30)

When the [Constitutional Convention](/wiki/Constitutional_Convention_(United_States) "Constitutional Convention (United States)") convened in May 1787, the 12 state delegations in attendance ([Rhode Island](/wiki/Rhode_Island "Rhode Island") did not send delegates) brought with them an accumulated experience over a diverse set of institutional arrangements between legislative and executive branches from within their respective state governments. Heading into the [2019–20 season](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_NHL_season "2019–20 NHL season"), the Flyers hired coach [Alain Vigneault](/wiki/Alain_Vigneault "Alain Vigneault") and signed forward [Kevin Hayes](/wiki/Kevin_Hayes_(ice_hockey) "Kevin Hayes (ice hockey)") in the hopes of bringing the team to cup contender status again. Opening day took place in the Czech Republic, Voracek's birthplace. The Flyers beat the Blackhawks 4–2. The Flyers started off the season very well, tying a team record for the best November in team history with a record of 10–3–4.[[50]](#cite_note-53) The Flyers produced consistent, cohesive hockey throughout the season. One of the most notable progressions in the team was the chemistry of the team and the success of the second line, which consisted of [Scott Laughton](/wiki/Scott_Laughton "Scott Laughton"), Kevin Hayes, and [Travis Konecny](/wiki/Travis_Konecny "Travis Konecny"). In February, the team pulled away from the pack of Wild-Card spot chasers and reached second place in the Metropolitan Division following a home win against the Rangers that put their February record at 9–3. The Flyers ended up with a nine-game winning streak, losing at home against the Boston Bruins, the NHL's points leader. The Flyers were scheduled to play at Tampa Bay on March 12, but the NHL suspended all games earlier in the day due to [COVID-19 concerns](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_North_America "COVID-19 pandemic in North America"). The Flyers were second in the Metropolitan Division, only 1 point behind the Capitals.

The Flyers entered the [2020 playoffs](/wiki/2020_Stanley_Cup_playoffs "2020 Stanley Cup playoffs") "bubble" in Toronto as the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference, meaning they had clinched a playoff appearance and were to play in a seeding round-robin between the top four teams of the conference. Main article: [Hewlett-Packard § History](/wiki/Hewlett-Packard#History "Hewlett-Packard")

Hewlett-Packard was founded in 1939 by [Bill Hewlett](/wiki/Bill_Hewlett "Bill Hewlett") and [David Packard](/wiki/David_Packard "David Packard"), who both graduated with degrees in [electrical engineering](/wiki/Electrical_engineering "Electrical engineering") from [Stanford University](/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University") in 1935. The company started off in the [HP Garage](/wiki/HP_Garage "HP Garage") in [Palo Alto, California](/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California").

In March 2015, HP announced that [Bang & Olufsen](/wiki/Bang_%26_Olufsen "Bang & Olufsen") would become the company's new premium audio partner for its computers and other devices. This replaced the partnership with [Beats Electronics](/wiki/Beats_Electronics "Beats Electronics") that ended upon being acquired by [Apple Inc.](/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc.") in 2014.[[6]](#cite_note-cnet-bando-6)

On November 1, 2015, Hewlett-Packard was split into two companies. Its personal computer and printer businesses became HP Inc., while its enterprise business became [Hewlett Packard Enterprise](/wiki/Hewlett_Packard_Enterprise "Hewlett Packard Enterprise"). The split was structured so that Hewlett-Packard changed its name to HP Inc. and spun off Hewlett Packard Enterprise as a new publicly traded company. HP Inc. retains Hewlett-Packard's pre-2015 stock price history and its former stock ticker symbol, HPQ, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise trades under its own symbol, HPE.[[3]](#cite_note-Chan-3)[[4]](#cite_note-Darrow-4)[[7]](#cite_note-7)

British Shorthair :: Breed registration :: Popularity :: chunk_0004
The British Shorthair publicity from 19th and 20th century cat shows helped British Shorthairs become one of the most popular pet cat breeds today. For example, in the 1980s, the British Shorthair was featured in competition by the CFA, which led to an increased demand for British Shorthairs as household pets. As of 2023, the British Shorthair ranks as the 6th most popular cat breed in the United States.[[10]](#cite_note-10) According to the GCCF's 2024 registry data, it is once again the most popular pedigreed breed in its native country, accounting for about half of the annually registered kittens.[[1]](#cite_note-GCCFprof-1)[[11]](#cite_note-11) And it has held the title of the UK's most popular cat breed for decades.[[12]](#cite_note-12)[[13]](#cite_note-13) In the 2024 statistics of [FIFe](/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_F%C3%A9line "Fédération Internationale Féline"), one of the major global [cat registries](/wiki/Cat_registries "Cat registries"), the breed ranked at position 2 out of 54 breeds in popularity, comprising 16.9% of their total registered kittens that year, which translates to 16.278 cats.[[14]](#cite_note-FIFestat-14)
